How to Write a
Response/Reaction Essay





                                                                                                                                   1

Outline

What is a response/reaction essay?
How is a response essay organized?
How to write the introduction paragraph
How to write a body paragraph
How to write a conclusion





                                                                                                                                       2

What is a response/reaction essay?

A response or reaction essay is typically a 2-5 page document in which the writer
   responds to an article, a book, or a video.


To write a response essay, you need to read an article (or watch a video) and
   explain your own thoughts about it. Evaluate what you think about the issue and
   relate it to your own experiences or other things you have read.


A response essay may consist of your personal reactions and impressions. It may
   also be a critique or evaluation of the article you’ve read. You may examine ideas
   that you agree or disagree with.





                                                                                                                                       3

What is a response/reaction essay?


A good response essay is persuasive; it should cite facts, examples, and personal
   experience that either refutes or supports the article you’re responding to,
  depending on your stance.


It should be written from the first person point of view, which means that you can
  and should use phrases like “I think” and “I believe” when writing.





                                                                                                                                       4

How is a response essay organized?

A typical way to write a response essay is to first summarize the work you’re
   reacting to and then discuss your reactions. It may have the following format:


Introduction Paragraph: Introduce the title of the work and summarize it.
   Include a thesis statement that explains your overall reaction.
Body Paragraph 1: First reaction (e.g., Do you agree or disagree?)
Body Paragraph 2: Second reaction (e.g., What does it remind you of?)
Body Paragraphs 3: Third reaction (e.g., Do you have a different perspective?)
Concluding Paragraph: Summarize your reactions.





                                                                                                                                       5

How to write the introduction paragraph

The first sentence of the introduction paragraph should mention the author and
    title of the work to which you are responding to.


Give a brief summary of the work or the part of the work that you are responding
   to.


The last sentence of your introductory paragraph should contain a thesis
   statement.





                                                                                                                                       6

How to write the introduction paragraph

In Ralph Rigman’s book The Whisper of Names, he writes about his experiences growing
up in the rural south of the country and how he envisions it possible to recreate the past
wealth. His key points in this narrative and political story were that policy changes have
resulted in the decline of southern wealth, and that continued machination would result in
the downfall of the human race. He argues that by implementing more protectionist
policies, agricultural and industrial jobs would return to the country and enable the
poverty-stricken communities. Despite his arguments that policy changes have contributed
most to the decline of the south, I believe that his lack of recognition of contribution of
social factors makes this book highly unbelievable.


Notice that the title and author of the work are mentioned at the beginning. The writer states
their reaction and the reason for the reaction in the thesis statement.





                                                                                                                                       7

How to write a body paragraph

In the body, you can write about the following with supporting details:

   1) Agreement or disagreement with the ideas in the work you’re responding to
   2) How the ideas in the work relate to your life, experiences, feelings, etc.
   3) How ideas in the work relate to other things you’ve read
   4) Your analysis of the author and audience
   5) Your evaluation of how this work tries to convince the reader and whether it is
   effective
   6) How the work relates to problems in our present-day world
   7) Whether the work has increased your understanding of a particular issue
   8) Whether the work has changed your perspective on a particular issue





                                                                                                                                        8

How to write a body paragraph

In this example, the writer supports their disagreement by laying out historical factors not
mentioned in the book. The writer’s response to the book is based on their own knowledge
about the topic.


In The Whisper of Names, Rigman suggests that policy changes favoring imported goods
have devastated the economy of the south. However, he fails to mention that much of the
wealth of the south had been held in land-owning prosperous families who had benefited
from the slave trade and subsequent cotton and tobacco industries. Throughout the early
20th century, these families continued to prosper under sharecropping laws. The civil rights
movement finally brought to light the injustices of racial inequality as well as the violation
of human rights that resulted in cheap labor that drove the south economy. Mr. Rigman
does not mention any of these factors in the book.





                                                                                                                                       9

How to write a conclusion

The last part of a response essay is an impressive conclusion. This is your final
   opportunity to gather up your thoughts and feelings and put them into a short
  summary. If you capture your raw emotions and why the piece made you feel that
  way, you will leave a lasting impression on the reader.


Start your conclusion by restating your reactions. Reaffirm the key points you
  made in the body paragraphs but avoid any new information. The conclusion
   should not include information not already discussed in the body.





                                                                                                                                       10

How to write a conclusion

In the following example, the writer restates their reactions by saying the film is
“enlightening and scary.” They also succinctly repeat three key points (see [1]-[3]) made
earlier in response to the film:


Overall, I not only enjoyed the film Miss Representation, but also learned a lot about
American media and its portrayal of women in society. It was very enlightening and
somewhat scary for future generations. [1] Women should not be always concerned with
their bodies for the sake a man’s pleasure but for their own happiness and that should be
celebrated. [2] Also women need to band together to find a voice and support one another
in finding each one’s individual voice. [3] Women have a very unique role in society as the
most prominent caregiver and that should be celebrated as well.
